- `data/wins.json`, `data/sections.json`, `data/uncounted-failures.json`, `data/predictions.json` — canonical WIN/prose/failure/prediction data. Committed by the decider after build/test.
- `data/kill-shots.json` — array of 7 KS-NNN kill-shot test entries (Sydney–Perth, Polaris, JFK–LHR, SAA, Eclipse 2026, NMP drift, stellar parallax). Schema documented in `monitor/prompts/reference/DATA-SCHEMAS.md` §kill-shots.json. **Status (verified 2026-07-09, ISS-2946):** this is live curmudgeon-review-target data (Phase 1 per-item review covers 'WINs, sections, prose, kill-shots' per `SCIENTIFIC-CONTEXT.md`) — NOT dead or superseded. However it is currently **disconnected from the build**: `build.js`/`build-scripts/*.js` do not read this file, and the `{{KS_TOTAL}}`/`{{KS_DECISIVE}}`/etc. placeholders documented in DATA-SCHEMAS.md do not exist anywhere in the codebase. The Kill Shots tab in `docs/index.html` (Part 5, Tests 1–7) is instead hand-authored static HTML that duplicates the same 7 tests. Spot-checked 2026-07-09: content is currently in sync (KS-001/002/006 verdicts and findings match Test 1/2/6 prose). Because the two copies are not build-linked, they can drift silently — a future edit to one won't propagate to the other. Treat `data/kill-shots.json` as the analytical source-of-record for curmudgeon review purposes; treat `docs/index.html` Part 5 as the current presentation source-of-record until/unless the build wiring described in DATA-SCHEMAS.md is implemented (untracked scope — not part of this BAU item).
patches.description: Add a file-map bullet documenting data/kill-shots.json: confirmed live curmudgeon-review-target data (not superseded/dead), but currently disconnected from build.js — the Kill Shots tab in docs/index.html is hand-authored HTML duplicating the same 7 tests rather than being generated from this JSON. Content spot-checked as currently in sync but drift-prone due to lack of build wiring.

tldr_evidence: data/kill-shots.json (7 KS-NNN entries) is actively used by the curmudgeon review pipeline (Phase 1 per-item review explicitly covers kill-shots), but is never read by build.js — the DATA-SCHEMAS.md-documented {{KS_TOTAL}} build placeholders do not exist in the codebase. The Kill Shots tab in docs/index.html is instead hand-written HTML that happens to currently match the JSON content.
tldr_verdict: Not orphaned, not superseded — it is live review data with an unfinished build integration. CLAUDE.md now documents this so future integrity runs stop re-flagging it as a mystery file, and future editors know both copies need updating until the build wiring lands.
investigation_notes: Checked build.js and build-scripts/*.js: zero references to kill-shots.json, KS_TOTAL, KS_DECISIVE, KS_MAJOR, KS_SUPPORTIVE, KS_STRAW_MAN_COUNT, KS_WAIT_AND_SEE_COUNT anywhere.
Checked monitor/prompts/reference/SCIENTIFIC-CONTEXT.md and curmudgeon.md: kill-shots ARE an active review target (killshot-* items in Phase 1 per-item review, priority-queue class=killshot-*).

Checked docs/index.html Kill Shots tab (Part 5): contains 7 hand-authored Test 1-7 blocks (ks-test-1..7 CSS class naming, not matching kill-shots.json section_anchor values ks-test-1..7 which DO match by coincidence/original-design but are not templated in).

Spot-checked KS-001 (Sydney-Perth, Misleading/major), KS-002 (Polaris, Not Demonstrated/supportive), KS-006 (NMP Drift, Refuted by Data/decisive, 39.9% error) against the corresponding hardcoded Test 1/2/6 HTML — verdicts, ratings, and key figures match.

Conclusion: kill-shots.json is the intended (per DATA-SCHEMAS.md) but never-implemented build source for the Kill Shots tab. It remains live/relevant as curmudgeon review-target data. No content correction needed; documentation gap only.
